body:
## Summary
Every inbound application is filed under a pipeline-entry PRIMARY KEY built from the applicant's email in clear text (`m-appl-jane-example-com-<job>`). That id is the ATS subject reference, the decision-chain candidateRef, the key on every event, and it survives erasure by design. Replace the derived id with an opaque surrogate and move the dedupe identity into an erasable, hashed `applicant_key` column with a partial unique index; erasure nulls it. As a direct consequence, the live bug where an erased applicant who re-applies RESURRECTS the anonymized row (re-activated, email backfilled, re-acknowledged) closes.

## Description
`applyDedupeKey` (apply-intake.ts:117) turns the normalized email into `appl-<email-with-hyphens>` and `createPipelineEntry` (db/pipeline.ts:1445-1452) makes it the row id. Identity resolution does not actually need that: `fileApplication` resolves a known applicant BEFORE building via `findApplicationByApplicant` (contact-based, application-filing.ts:261); the derived id only backstops two concurrent first filings. So the PII-bearing primary key buys one race guard and costs: the email in the ATS export (`ref: entry.id`), in the retained decision chain, in every server log line that names an entry (including the erasure path's own log at db/pipeline.ts:2513), and, worst, an erasure that can be undone. After anonymizeEntry nulls `contact`, a re-application misses the lookup, builds a fresh profile, regenerates the same id, lands on the erased row, flips a rejected status to active (1500-1506) and then, as a raced repeat promoted to 'channel' proof, backfills the email, re-sends an acknowledgement and renews consent on a record the candidate asked us to forget. The registry's retention standard says the opposite: a surrogate id stays, and an anonymised record is unreachable by every path that treats it as a person.

The move: a server-only `applicant-key.ts` computes a domain-separated sha256 of the normalized email (else normalized name; '' for anonymous). `createPipelineEntry` takes `applicantKey` instead of `dedupeKey`: it looks up an existing row by (workspace_id, job_id, applicant_key), else inserts with a random surrogate id (`m-<ws->rand-<job>`), and treats a UNIQUE violation on the partial index as the cross-connection race (re-select the winner, created:false - the db/tasks.ts:168 shape). `anonymizeEntry` adds `applicant_key = NULL` to its claim UPDATE, which is what makes an erased identity unmatchable. Recruiter/Match adds (candidateId-keyed ids) are untouched. Existing rows are NOT rewritten - their ids are referenced by the sealed decision chain - so legacy PII-bearing ids remain a named gap in the compliance doc; the change stops minting new ones and stops the resurrection for legacy rows too, because new filings no longer regenerate their ids.

Hot files: db/pipeline.ts and db/core.ts are shared with other contexts (pipeline-move-bulk-operations is in this cohort); the edits are confined to createPipelineEntry, the anonymizeEntry claim UPDATE, and one migration block.

## Flow
1. Write applicant-key.test.ts and application-filing-erasure.test.ts from the acceptance cases; run them red.
2. Add `applicant-key.ts` (node:crypto; server-only - apply-intake.ts stays client-importable) and delete applyDedupeKey + its re-export and its apply-intake.test.ts cases.
3. db/core.ts: `ALTER TABLE pipeline_entries ADD COLUMN applicant_key TEXT` + `CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_pipeline_applicant_key ON pipeline_entries (workspace_id, job_id, applicant_key) WHERE applicant_key IS NOT NULL` (all legacy rows NULL, so the index builds on any existing DB).
4. db/pipeline.ts: createPipelineEntry keyed lookup + surrogate id + UNIQUE catch; anonymizeEntry nulls applicant_key in the same guarded UPDATE.
5. application-filing.ts passes `applicantKey`; update application-filing.test.ts fixtures that pass `dedupeKey` literals.
6. Docs: candidates README (filing identity) and compliance README (erasure scope + the legacy-id gap).
7. Run the integration gate.

## Expected impact
New applications stop writing the applicant's email into a primary key that is exported to ATSs, sealed into the decision chain and printed in logs. Erasure becomes final for the re-application path: an erased candidate who applies again is a new applicant, never a re-contacted ghost of the old row, and no orphan profile is left behind. The race guard is preserved with a constraint instead of a naming trick.

## Evaluation
Claim: the entry id carries no applicant PII for new filings, the dedupe identity is erasable, and an erased entry cannot be re-opened, re-contacted or re-consented by a re-application.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - node:test cases above (applicant-key.test.ts, application-filing-erasure.test.ts, application-filing.test.ts) under npm run test:unit, plus the integration gate
Result: pending build
Gate: architecture

body:
## Summary
At interview and offer stage the status page tells the candidate to go look in their email. When the email is lost, they are stuck - and the server knows precisely what is waiting: a pending booking invite, an open offer with a deadline, an untaken AI interview. Project that as a three-field `nextAction` (kind, sentAt, expiresAt) on the status payload, render it as a 'Waiting on you' card with the deadline, and give the card one action: 'Send it to my email again', which re-dispatches the existing capability link to the address on file only.

## Description
The status route (api/status/[token]/route.ts:51-71) projects where the application stands but not what is expected of the candidate, which the registry's status-transparency golden path lists as permitted content. The data exists in three stores: schedule invites with a 7-day TTL (schedule-store.ts:384, schedule-slots.ts:45/67), open offers with `expiresAt` (offers-store.ts:309/110), and interview sessions created in status 'created' (db/interviews.ts:411/456/586).

The open backlog item proposes putting the interview/offer LINKS on the page. That is the wrong shape: the status link is forwardable, and the projection technique says its payload must be safe for a stranger. A forwarded status link that carries the offer token lets whoever holds it accept or decline the offer. So this card keeps the capability where it was issued - the inbox - and makes the page actionable anyway, the same doctrine r01 landed for link recovery (apply-link-recovery.ts): the resend goes only to `entry.contact`, at most once per entry per 24 hours (login-throttle), with copy chosen from the relay state alone so the response cannot probe for an address.

Pieces: a pure `candidate-next-action.ts` (precedence offer > booking > interview; expired or terminal -> null; `decideActionResend`; `resendMessageKey`), a server `candidate-next-action-server.ts` that reads the three stores for an entry and performs the resend by building the kind's link (publicBaseUrl + pinLinkLocale to the entry's comms locale) and calling the existing dispatcher, the status GET adding `nextAction`, a new `POST /api/status/[token]/resend` (per-IP+token rateLimit before any store read, coded refusals, `safeJsonError` on failure, auth posture public like its siblings), and a `StatusNextActionCard` in both themes from recipes (PANEL/BTN_*), dates via useFormatter. With no relay configured the card states the action and the deadline and says the team will reach out, with no resend button - never a promise the deployment cannot keep.

## Flow
1. Write candidate-next-action.test.ts from cases 1-7 and update the two key-list pins (case 8); run red.
2. Implement the pure module, then the server module over the three stores and the three existing dispatchers.
3. Add `nextAction` to the status GET; add the resend route with its limiter; add the limiter to app/api/rate-limit-contract.test.ts; `npm run api:docs` for the reference row.
4. StatusNextActionCard + a two-line mount in StatusClient (between the timeline and the decisions section); catalog keys in en/cs/de/fr in one locked commit (no em dashes).
5. Compliance README: what the status payload now carries and why the token never does.
6. Integration gate; check both themes.

## Expected impact
The two stages with the highest candidate stakes stop being dead ends. A candidate who lost the invitation sees 'Book your interview - invitation sent 3 Sep, open until 10 Sep' and gets it back in one click; an offer shows its deadline on the page the candidate already bookmarks. This removes the 'any update? I can't find the email' chase the golden path names as the real operating cost, without widening what a forwarded status link can do.

## Evaluation
Claim: the status payload states the pending candidate action with its deadline and never a capability; the resend door re-delivers only to the address on file, once per entry per day, without revealing whether one exists.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - node:test (candidate-next-action.test.ts, status-letter.test.ts, status-recording.test.ts, rate-limit-contract.test.ts) under npm run test:unit, plus i18n:check, api:check and the integration gate
Result: pending build
Gate: contract
